## Rationale

Input resistance (R_in) is the reciprocal of the total resting membrane conductance, G_rest = ḡ_leak × A, where A is total membrane area and ḡ_leak is the specific (per-unit-area) resting conductance. Any molecular explanation of R_in variation must therefore act through one of two levers: **cell size** or the **density of tonically open ("leak") channels**.

Patch-seq studies of adult mouse V1 have established that R_in is among the electrophysiological features most strongly structured by transcriptomic identity (Cadwell et al. 2016; Fuzik et al. 2016; Gouwens et al. 2020; Scala et al. 2021): Pvalb-lineage basket/chandelier cells are large, low-R_in neurons (~50–120 MΩ); Sst-lineage Martinotti cells are intermediate (~150–350 MΩ); CGE-derived Vip and Lamp5 cells are small, high-R_in neurons (~200–600 MΩ). R_in strongly anti-correlates with capacitance, so cell size — a cell-state property fixed by lineage programs (e.g., Lhx6-dependent MGE differentiation) — explains much of the between-class variance. The mechanistically open question is the molecular identity of the **specific leak conductance**, i.e., "leakiness per unit membrane."

The only channel family whose dedicated physiological role is the resting leak is the **two-pore-domain K+ (K2P/KCNK) family**: tonically open, weakly voltage-dependent, established determinants of resting potential and input resistance (Goldstein et al. 2001; Enyedi & Czirják 2010). The alternatives are less compelling as the class axis: Kcnc1/Kv3.1 (the canonical Pvalb marker) activates only above ~−20 mV and cannot set resting conductance; Hcn1/Ih shapes sag and modulates R_in (Robinson & Siegelbaum 2003), but the cells with the largest Ih (many Sst Martinotti cells) are *not* the lowest-R_in cells, so Ih cannot drive the main class axis; Kcna1/Kv1 window current is minimal at −70 mV; NALCN provides a Na⁺ leak (Lu et al. 2007) and remains a live but distinguishable alternative. In the Allen single-cell atlas, K2P genes are among the ion-channel genes most differentially expressed across cortical interneuron transcriptomic types (Tasic et al. 2018), with **Kcnk12 (THIK-2)** a prominent differentially expressed member in GABAergic types — yet its functional contribution to neuronal R_in has never been tested.

## Committed hypothesis

**The size-independent variation in input resistance among adult mouse V1 GABAergic interneurons is caused by transcriptomic-class-specific dosage of KCNK two-pore-domain leak K⁺ channels — lead candidate Kcnk12 (THIK-2) — such that higher K2P expression yields a larger tonic K⁺ leak conductance and lower R_in.** The transcriptomic class (Pvalb/Sst/Vip/Lamp5 lineage state) is the upstream cell state that coordinates both cell size and K2P expression. Formally: R_in ≈ [A·(g_K2P + g_other)]⁻¹, with g_K2P varying across classes.

## Experimentally testable predictions

1. **Patch-seq partial regression:** R_in ~ capacitance + Kcnk12 counts (or a K2P expression module). Predict a significant *negative* partial coefficient for Kcnk12 within and across transcriptomic types; no negative partial coefficient for high-threshold channels (Kcnc1) once class is controlled.
2. **Loss of function:** AAV-CRISPRi/shRNA knockdown of Kcnk12 in V1 interneurons (or Kcnk12-null mice) raises R_in preferentially in high-expressing classes. If THIK-2 proves ER-retained/non-functional in these cells (a known caveat from heterologous expression work), the identical test falls to the next-ranked K2P members within the same mechanism — Kcnk2/TREK-1 or Kcnk9/TASK-3, for which KO mice and blockers (e.g., spadin) exist.
3. **Gain of function:** Kcnk12 overexpression in a low-expressing, high-R_in class (Vip/Lamp5) decreases R_in.
4. **Mechanistic fingerprint:** K⁺-leak blockade must *depolarize* the resting potential while increasing R_in; a NALCN mechanism would *hyperpolarize*; ZD7288 (Ih) would remove sag. Acute-slice pharmacology with these signatures cleanly separates the candidate mechanisms.

## Established vs. novel

Established (a): the class structure of R_in in V1 interneurons (Gouwens et al. 2020; Scala et al. 2021); K2P channels as the molecular leak (Enyedi & Czirják 2010); single-neuron gene–ephys correlation methodology (Cadwell et al. 2016; Fuzik et al. 2016). **New and testable (b): the specific causal claim that Kcnk12/K2P dosage is a principal, size-independent determinant of R_in variation among cortical GABAergic interneurons.** My conclusion is therefore primarily (b), built on established (a) foundations.

Key references: Cadwell et al., Nat Biotechnol 34:199–213 (2016); Fuzik et al., Nat Commun 7:11477 (2016); Gouwens et al., Nature 586:78–85 (2020); Scala et al., Nat Neurosci 24:482–492 (2021); Tasic et al., Cell 174:765–783 (2018); Goldstein et al., Nat Rev Neurosci 2:175–184 (2001); Enyedi & Czirják, Physiol Rev 90:559–573 (2010); Lu et al., Cell 129:371–383 (2007); Robinson & Siegelbaum, Annu Rev Physiol 65:453–480 (2003); Gupta et al., Science 287:273–278 (2000); Kawaguchi & Kubota, Cereb Cortex 7:476–486 (1997).
